lines.text: Here's something that surprises people. The to-do list an agent shows you is written by the model, for itself.

lines.text: It's a tool call, like any other. The model writes a call with the list in it: each step, and for each one, whether it's waiting, under way, or done.

lines.text: And the harness runs what, exactly?
Nothing. There's no command behind it. The harness keeps the list and draws it for you. Here, that's the checklist board. In your agent, it's a list beside the conversation.

lines.text: So the model calls a tool whose whole job is taking notes.

Exactly that. Remember, the model only ever writes text. If it wants something written down where it'll see it again, it has to write it into the conversation. A to-do call is a tidy, structured way of doing that, and the harness can show it to you as a bonus.

lines.text: How does each agent do it?

Claude Code has two tools for it, TaskCreate and TaskUpdate, and Ctrl+T shows the list. Codex has update_plan: a list of steps, each one pending, in progress or completed. Copilot in VS Code has a todos tool, and shows the list at the top of the Chat view.

lines.text: So I'll see a list every time.

Not necessarily, and this part is recent. Claude Code leaves those tools out on its newest models, unless you switch them back on with a setting. And since September twenty twenty-six, Codex's update_plan is off until you turn it on in its config file.

lines.text: A list isn't free. Every tool the model is offered costs tokens on every turn, just to describe it. And newer models keep track of a long task without writing one down. Where the list lives, and what it costs, is the last card of this trip.
